title: Microsoft Teams: voice phishing detection for external calls
summary: Hold: the briefing treats Defender visibility for calls reported as not a security concern as an unanswered question, although Microsoft documents submission metadata and default alerts for those reports. The roadmap facts and voice phishing policy command are supported; uncertainty about automatic detection alerts reaching Defender remains legitimate.

claims.where: Open questions: Defender portal, automatic alert
claims.claim: Whether an automatic voice phishing detection alert sends information to Defender is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams voice phishing detection audio processing retention audit logs Scam Suspected outbound calls. Read Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy and submissions-teams: Defender visibility is documented for user reports, not for this detector's automatic alerts.

claims.where: Open questions: Defender portal, report as not a security concern
claims.claim: Whether the Defender portal receives anything when a user reports a flagged call as not a security concern is left as unpublished.
claims.quote: Metadata from the reported Teams items (for example, senders/callers, recipients, reported by, meeting and participant details, and item details) is available on the User reported tab on the Submissions page.
claims.fix: Replace the final Open questions bullet with: 'Does the Defender portal receive anything automatically when a voice phishing detection alert is raised?' Remove the user-report branch: https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/submissions-teams documents report metadata in Submissions and says the 'Teams call reported by user as a not security risk' alert policy generates alerts by default.
